name: Farro bowls with braised chicken, chard, and pickled fennel
intro: What the weekend braise turns into midweek: nutty, chewy farro, the chicken pulled off the bone and warmed in its leeks and juices, chard wilted in, and the jar on top.
needs: ¾ cup farro, whole or semi-pearled
4 leftover braised chicken thighs, with their leeks and juices
½ bunch Swiss chard, stems chopped, leaves torn

steps.text: Simmer the farro in a big pot of salted water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew. Pearled farro is faster — start checking at 15 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, pull the chicken off the bones in big pieces and discard the bones. Keep the skin if you like it.
Warm the leeks and juices from the braise in a skillet over medium. Add the chard stems and cook until tender, then the chicken and the chard leaves until the leaves wilt and everything is hot.
Farro in bowls, the chicken and greens over it with plenty of juice, pickled fennel, Parmesan, black pepper, and lemon.

how_it_works: Braise once, eat twice: the juices left in the pot are the best sauce of the week, and farro is the grain built to soak them up without going soft. Farro is a whole grain when it's whole or semi-pearled; pearled farro cooks faster because most of the bran has been polished off.
swaps: Rice instead of farro, if that's what's in the pantry.
Leftover thighs from the one-pot chicken and white beans.
leftovers: Cooked farro keeps four days in the fridge; make a double batch and use it under the flat iron or the soup.

nutrition.serving: Half the recipe: two braised thighs with their leeks and juices, about 1 cup cooked farro, chard, and Parmesan.
nutrition.excludes: Nothing. These are the braise's leftovers, so don't count them twice.
